text:
deploy-bot: Deploy started: v2.4.1 -> prod canary 10% (hosts: canary-1, canary-2). changelist: feat/streaming-kv-cache + hotfix/quantize-ops

sara: seeing a spike in 5xxs hitting /api/generate from canary-1, ~3.8% over last 2m :rotating_light:

mike: can you paste logs? grep for stack traces or OOMs?

sara: logs show repeated 'CUDA OOM' and a few 'kernel launch failed' on canary-1. no traceback in app logs yet.

olivia: oncall-bot alert: errors > 3% for 3m on service inference-api. Runbook ROLLBACK-001: if sustained >=3% for 5m -> auto rollback, otherwise manual review. We're at 3m but not 5m yet.

mike: I'd prefer manual rollback given OOMs. Auto-rollback would help but we should pin version and drain traffic only after confirming root cause isn't infra flake.

sara: agree. I'll pin traffic to v2.3 for canary hosts and stop further promotions. starting pin now.

deploy-bot: Action: traffic_policy update -> pinned version v2.3 for canary-1, canary-2. (user: sara)

mike: running rollback script to revert model binary and restart runtimes on canary-1. cmd: 
```
./scripts/rollback_prod.sh --targets canary-1 --from v2.4.1 --to v2.3 --restart
```

mike: script returned exit 0, restarted runtime, healthchecks passing.

sara: metrics check: 5xx down to 0.4% on canary-1 within 90s, latency back to baseline.

olivia: good. Since we did manual rollback, we should file an incident note and decide if we want to enable auto-rollback for OOM-class errors.

emma-cs: cc support/CS — flagging that some customers saw generation failures during the window, creating a support ticket summary.

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2025-077 - prod canary OOM during v2.4.1 rollout. Assigned to eng-runtime.

mike: next steps: reproduce in staging with same binary + smaller batch sizes, instrument allocator logging, and isolate whether it's a kernel selection regression. I'll open PR for rollback-telemetry.

sara: communications: I'll post short note in #product (and update release notes) that v2.4.1 rollout paused due to infra regression; pinning to v2.3 for stability.

olivia: nice work. If staging repro is quick, we can try a guarded re-deploy with reduced batch sizes and canary at 5% only after confirmation. For now, monitoring will remain on high alert for 2 hours.

sara: closing the thread for now. if anything else pops, ping @olivia and @mike. :thumbsup:
